newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore jet fuel strong, diesel traded lower.
newsitem.headline: Singapore jet fuel strong, diesel traded lower.

text.p: Singapore oil products were mixed on on Wednesday with jet fuel rallying on tight supplies, while physical gas oil traded slightly lower, traders said.

Physical jet fuel was sold by a US trader to a Dutch trader at $31.75, a new-post winter high for Dec 5-9 lifting fob. But traders said this was five cents under swaps kerosene values. They said the abundance of jet fuel over the past month prompted Singapore refiners to maximise gas oil production recently, causing jet supplies to tighten along with purchases from Japan. The most recent cargo Japan bought was a 30,000-tonne lot for mid-December delivery at $1.75 a barrel to Singapore quotes c+f.
But traders are cautious about further Japanese demand as its weather during December-February are forecast as average, compared with the harsh winter last year.

Physical gas oil was traded twice at $30.50 per barrel for mid-December lifting fob, each involving 150,000-barrel cargoes. These were lower than the last traded price of $30.80. But swaps gas oil firmed on crude strength with December quoted at $30.50/$30.60, up 30 cents from Tuesday. Traders said the market has not reacted to news of a possible strike by Kuwaiti oil workers at the Mina al-Ahmadi export terminal. The union and Kuwait National Petroleum Corp are now talking.

Naphtha firmed on crudes with swaps for December rising to $22.90/$23.10 a barrel from $22.65/$22.75 Tuesday. Results from Taiwan's import term tender for 1997 for N+A are due Thursday, an official said. Traders said Taiwan may conclude awards with two sellers for a cargo each a month or quarter at $3.45 to $4.00 a barrel over Singapore quotes c+f Taiwan. They said the term premium for 1996 was around $3.75 a barrel. Mostly buyers

were seen in the gasoline market at slightly firmer prices - 95-octane bid at $25.40-$25.50, up from Tuesday's deal at $25.40. A 97-octane cargo was heard traded at $26.15 for December 10-14 lifting.--Singapore Newsroom (+65-870-3084)
